title: Commentaries of Proclus on Euclid, Vol. 2
author: Proclus (Taylor trans)
description: The Philosophical and Mathematical Commentaries of Proclus on the First Book of Euclid's Elements, Volume 2, translated by Thomas Taylor (London, 1788-89; reissued 1792), completing his English version with Proclus's detailed commentary on the postulates, axioms and propositions of Euclid's first book, up to the Pythagorean theorem and its converse. Proclus explains each proof, records alternative demonstrations and objections from earlier geometers such as Heron, Posidonius, Geminus and Pappus, and repeatedly draws out the theological and symbolic meaning of geometrical figures, the point, line, circle, angle, triangle and square, as images of divine principles and of the soul's procession and return. Taylor adds his own translations and notes, including material on Pythagorean and Platonic mathematics. Together with Volume 1, it shows how late antique Platonists treated mathematics as a ladder to the divine and is a key source for the Neoplatonic philosophy of geometry.
